standard_prerequisites.name: Differential graded category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A category enriched in graded R-modules with a differential on each Hom complex for which composition satisfies the Leibniz rule.
standard_prerequisites.use: The composition c and its Leibniz rule are used at source lines 5126-5140.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dg (A,B)-bimodule and its Hom functor
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a dg (A,B)-bimodule N the assignments on objects and on Hom complexes that make the Hom out of N into an A-module a dg functor.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the construction whose compatibility with differentials the proof establishes (source lines 5117-5125, 5131-5134).

standard_prerequisites.name: Induced functors on the module and homotopy categories
standard_prerequisites.statement: A functor of dg categories that is compatible with differentials induces functors between the associated module categories and between their homotopy categories (the author's lemma lemma-functorial, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked in the statement itself to pass from the dg functor to the functors on Mod and on K(Mod) (source line 5113).

core_obligations: Set up the comparison: note that the construction is already a functor of graded categories and introduce the Hom complexes H_12, H_1 and H_2 together with the composition c of the dg category (source lines 5117-5130).

Compute both differentials: for a homogeneous f of degree n describe the image c_f of f, compute the differential of c_f in the Hom complex out of the A-module as d composed with c_f minus the signed composition with d, and use the Leibniz rule for c to expand d(c(f,g)) (source lines 5131-5141).

Compare and conclude: cancel the two copies of the term c(f, dg) to obtain (d c_f)(g) = c(df, g), i.e. that the construction sends df to the differential of the image, so the dg functor is compatible with differentials; then apply the retained lemma lemma-functorial to obtain the functors on the module and homotopy categories (source lines 5142-5151).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to compatibility with differentials and introduce H_12, H_1, H_2 and the composition c.
Take homogeneous f of degree n, write its image c_f, and expand both the differential of c_f and d(c(f,g)).
Cancel the common term to get (d c_f)(g) = c(df, g), completing the compatibility and yielding the induced functors.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-hom at source lines 5095-5114: for a ring R, dg algebras (A,d) and (B,d) over R and a dg (A,B)-bimodule N, the construction sending a dg B-module to the dg A-module of its morphisms from N is a functor of dg categories, and hence induces functors on the module category and on the homotopy category. The proof at source lines 5116-5152 is a compatibility computation that is the actual content: it sets up the three Hom complexes H_12, H_1, H_2, recalls the composition morphism c of the dg category, takes a homogeneous element f of H_12 of degree n, computes the differential of the induced map c_f on both sides, and compares them term by term using the Leibniz rule for c and the cancellation of the two copies of the c(f, dg) term. The statement concentrates everything into the phrase that the construction above defines a functor; the proof is where the sign bookkeeping and the Leibniz rule are actually carried out, and it is essential that the differential on the Hom complex involves the sign (-1)^n. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
